test.title: Something you do to stay organised

document.cue: Describe something you do to stay organised.

text: The habit I'd like to describe is planning my week every Sunday evening. It takes me about twenty minutes, and I do it with a paper notebook and a cup of tea, usually after dinner when the flat is quiet.

I started about three years ago, in my second year at university, when I was working part-time and kept forgetting deadlines. After missing an important assignment by one day, which cost me a lot of marks, I decided I needed a system rather than relying on my memory.

My method is quite simple. First I write down all my fixed commitments, like lectures and work shifts. Then I list everything I need to finish that week and choose the three most important tasks, which I highlight in yellow. Every evening I spend two minutes ticking things off and moving anything unfinished to the next day.

It helps because I can see the whole week at a glance, so I rarely get surprised by a deadline anymore, and I feel much less anxious. I've tried planning apps too, but writing by hand makes me think more carefully about what's realistic, and there are no notifications to distract me.
I'd definitely recommend it, especially to students who feel constantly behind.
